claims.text: A machine-learning-based, data-driven optimization approach can rapidly identify RHEA compositions combining intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
The machine-learning approach will outperform traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods in speed and targeted properties.
RHEAs have a vast compositional design space arising from multiple principal refractory elements.
Existing experimental and computational datasets for the RHEA design space are sparse.
A machine-learning model can be trained by combining historical experiments, CALPHAD outputs, and limited simulation results.
The resulting model can rapidly screen RHEA compositions for low density, high strength, and high ductility.
A compositional search range of 5–50 at.% per element is suitable for the proposed refractory-alloy screening.
The approach is implemented under laboratory-controlled synthesis and testing conditions.
Promising compositions will form a desirable microstructure such as a single BCC phase or mixed phases containing coherent precipitates.
The desirable phase and precipitate structure intrinsically mediates better mechanical properties and reduced weight.
Integrating thermodynamic models with data-driven optimization can exploit composition–property patterns to select alloys.
Balancing phase stability, lattice distortion, and density through optimization improves mechanical performance.
The approach will produce experimentally validated RHEAs with improved strength and ductility and lower density than alloys designed solely by traditional simulations.
Current thermo-kinetic and simulation approaches require extensive computational resources and time to scan the compositional space.
The method's success is limited by the quality and quantity of available data.
Predictions outside the explored refractory-element composition ranges may be unreliable.
The reliability of the model's predictions depends on the representativeness of its training dataset.
